# Kyoto 4-Day Vegetarian-Friendly Trip Plan

A moderate-pace Kyoto plan focused on neighborhoods, one cultural highlight per day, mostly public transit, and budget control for 2 adults. I’m assuming you want comfortable mid-range meals, standard transit passes, and no paid private guide.

## Day-by-Day Kyoto Neighborhood Itinerary
### Day 1: Higashiyama + Gion
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- Morning: Start in **Higashiyama** with a slow walk through Sannenzaka and Ninenzaka; visit **Kiyomizu-dera** as the day’s cultural anchor.
- Afternoon: Continue to **Yasaka Shrine** and the **Maruyama Park** area; keep the pace light with tea or dessert stops.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/f/f8/A199_Japan_Kyoto_Maruyama_Park_Gion_Ar%C3%A9a_%284764445344%29.jpg Alt=Afternoon: Continue to **Yasaka Shrine** and the **Maruyama Park** area; keep the pace light with tea or dessert stops, Kyoto, Japan
- Evening: Explore **Gion** lanes at dusk; good for atmosphere, photos, and an early dinner.
- Food: Vegetarian set meal or tofu kaiseki; ask for **gluten-free soy sauce** or sauces on the side.

### Day 2: Arashiyama + Sagano
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- Morning: Head to **Arashiyama** early for **Tenryu-ji** and the bamboo grove before crowds build.
- Afternoon: Walk the **Togetsukyo Bridge** area and riverside paths; keep optional add-ons flexible.
- Evening: Return to central Kyoto for a relaxed neighborhood dinner around **Shijo-Kawaramachi**.
- Food: Look for tofu, yuba, soba, rice bowls, and vegetable tempura; confirm **buckwheat soba** is 100% buckwheat if gluten is a concern.

### Day 3: Central Kyoto + Nishiki + Teramachi
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/shop.svg
- Morning: Visit **Nishiki Market** for snack browsing and local ingredients; focus on vegetarian-friendly stalls.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/e5/A_store_at_Nishiki_market%2C_Kyoto%2C_Japan.jpg Alt=Morning: Visit **Nishiki Market** for snack browsing and local ingredients; focus on vegetarian-friendly stalls, Kyoto, Japan
- Afternoon: Spend time in **Teramachi** and **Shinkyogoku** for shopping, cafés, and an easy indoor break.
- Evening: Choose a cultural activity such as a **tea ceremony** or a small temple visit in the central district.
- Food: Best day for flexible grazing; carry a translation card for gluten-free needs and avoid shared fryers.

### Day 4: Northern Kyoto + Okazaki
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/map.svg
- Morning: Visit **Kinkaku-ji** early, then move toward the north for a calm start.
- Afternoon: Continue to **Okazaki** for the **Kyoto City KYOCERA Museum of Art** or nearby gardens.
- Evening: End in **Downtown Kyoto** for a final dinner and souvenir shopping.
- Food: Choose a vegetable-forward dinner near the city center; many places can accommodate tofu and rice-based dishes more easily than gluten-free noodles.

## Budget and Spending Plan
### Estimated Daily Spend for 2 Adults
| Day | Neighborhood Focus | Transit | Food | Entry/Activity | Total |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Day 1 | Higashiyama + Gion | USD 12 | USD 70 | USD 20 | USD 102 |
| Day 2 | Arashiyama + Sagano | USD 14 | USD 75 | USD 25 | USD 114 |
| Day 3 | Central Kyoto + Nishiki | USD 10 | USD 85 | USD 35 | USD 130 |
| Day 4 | Northern Kyoto + Okazaki | USD 16 | USD 70 | USD 35 | USD 121 |

- **Estimated trip total:** **USD 467**
- **Budget remaining:** **USD 1,333** for nicer meals, shopping, taxis when needed, extra admissions, or a higher hotel category
- This leaves plenty of room under your **USD 1,800** target even with a comfortable hotel

## Getting Around Kyoto Smoothly
- Use **IC transit cards** like ICOCA or Suica for buses and trains.
- Prefer **subway + train** over buses during rush periods; buses can be slow and crowded.
- Group sights by neighborhood to reduce transfers:
  - **Higashiyama/Gion** on one day
  - **Arashiyama** on one day
  - **Central Kyoto** on one day
  - **Northern Kyoto/Okazaki** on one day
- Start early for major sights to avoid queues and make walking easier.
- For gluten-free needs, carry a short note in Japanese and ask about:
  - soy sauce
  - tempura batter
  - noodle broths
  - shared fryers
- Many vegetarian dishes are available, but **dashi** may contain fish even in “vegetable-looking” dishes.
- Keep one flexible meal per day for convenience rather than planning every stop too tightly.
